title: Favorite saxophonists and playing the melody
summary: Johnson's favorites away from New Orleans; he values hearing the melody.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Coleman Hawkins and the great saxophonists

blocks.x: It's a different pitch there, a different key rhythm. Alright. Do you have any favorites on saxophone away from New Orleans? Some other guys that you like? Oh yeah.
Johnny Hodges and Connie Barrett and Sancho. Oh yeah.
My two men are, what I was saying before, Paul Bourne and Bigard. Those are your standard men. In other words, they play something you know what they're playing.
You must have always liked New Collington's band. Oh yeah, yes. I guess.

You like those men. Oh yeah. You understand what they're playing, as I say, before they play a melody and the next chorus they play them, they leave the melody of Renown and Run All Around, but you still can understand that melody is right there. They have some nowadays that they play even though they're well-made man. They play them. Who'd have thought it or something. Playing what?
Well you believe in hearing the tune, in other words, it should be there one way or another. That's right. I have a very good year.

If a number is played and I don't know it, I'll feel around for it a little bit. And then most second choruses, I'm most assured that eventually I will get it. Of course, I have a good year. I can write, I can read music.
